signals.title: USD/JPY — Macro Alignment vs Crowded Specs
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.06, holding above its SMA20 at 156.79 while remaining below the SMA50/200 cluster. BoJ holds at 1.25%. CFTC positioning shows JPY Leveraged Funds net long at +20,069 contracts (pctl 95, z +1.57), signaling a crowded speculative long position after a massive WoW shift of +73,324 contracts. Options markets aggressively hedge downside exposure, with 25d Risk Reversals printing a heavy -1.88 put skew, while USD/JPY VRP sits negative at -1.9% (IV 8.0% vs HV30 9.9%), reflecting thin options supply. This establishes an asymmetric setup where crowded spec longs and options downside hedges conflict with persistent underlying carry. Trade bias: Bullish USD/JPY, carry support outweighs split BOJ hike impact. Catalyst: ECB President Lagarde speech at 11:00 UTC and US 2Y Note Auction at 17:00 UTC. Risk: VIX spikes above 25 or BOJ intervention rhetoric accelerates, forcing a rapid liquidation of carry positions.

signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry
signals.text: AUD/JPY trades at 111.96, benefiting from a dominant G10 cross-currency divergence where AUD is the strongest G10 currency (1W avg +0.297% across 4 pairs) and JPY is the weakest (1W avg -0.622% across 7 pairs), producing a 0.919% bilateral spread. Hawkish RBA bets—supported by Australian Big Four banks aligning on a September hike to 4.60%—boost AUD sentiment alongside a solid Economic Surprise Index reading of +14.2. RBA at 4.35% vs BOJ at 1.25% creates a +310bp rate differential (+337bp on AONIA vs TONA OIS), giving AUD/JPY the highest carry advantage in the G10 space. CFTC data shows AUD Leveraged Funds net long at +59,299 contracts (pctl 97, z +2.11), marking a crowded institutional position that reflects sustained momentum. Trade bias: Long AUD/JPY, driven by G10 performance spread and carry yield advantage. Catalyst: next RBA meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) on 29 September. Risk: Global risk-off sentiment triggers a sharp unwind of crowded AUD longs.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Crowded Long vs Retail Sentiment
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7132, sitting below its SMA20 at 0.7168 but above the SMA50 at 0.7087. RBA at 4.35% vs Fed at 4.00% creates a -35bp rate differential (-50bp on OIS), favoring AUD carry over USD. CFTC data reports AUD Leveraged Funds net long at +59,299 contracts (pctl 97, z +2.11), indicating an extreme, crowded institutional long position at the top of its 52-week historical range. Meanwhile, Retail sentiment data retail sentiment is balanced at 49% long / 51% short, showing no retail divergence and leaving institutional positioning to drive price action. 1M ATM IV sits at 6.5% vs HV30 of 5.5%, generating a +1.0% VRP that indicates modest option demand for downside protection. Trade bias: Neutral/Caution AUD/USD, crowded spec long limits fresh upside momentum near SMA20. Catalyst: Next RBA policy meeting on 29 September. Risk: Australia employment data upside surprise forces further hawkish RBA repricing.

signals.title: USD/CHF — Policy Rate Differential + ESI
signals.text: USD/CHF trades at 0.8233, maintaining a clear bullish structure above its SMA20 (0.8117), SMA50 (0.8108), and SMA200 (0.7939). Fed at 4.00% vs SNB at 0.00% generates a massive +400bp rate differential, providing structural carry support for USD. CFTC positioning shows CHF Leveraged Funds net short at -16,664 contracts (pctl 7, z -1.36), confirming strong speculative short exposure near historical deciles. However, Swiss economic data shows persistent strength with a CHF ESI of +22.1 (strongest in G10), while USD ESI sits near neutral at +2.2. USD/CHF options print an IV of 5.9% vs HV30 of 7.2% (VRP -1.2%), pointing to thin option supply and potential volatility expansion. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CHF, carry differential dominates despite robust Swiss macro data releases. Catalyst: SNB interest rate decision on 24 September. Risk: SNB delivers a hawkish surprise or intervenes directly to support CHF.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Moving Average Resistance + Negative Yield Spread Momentum
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3381, trapped below its moving average cluster with close at 1.3395, SMA20 at 1.3519, SMA50 at 1.3482, and SMA200 at 1.3455. Fed at 4.00% vs BoE at 3.75% creates a +25bp rate differential (+12bp on OIS), favoring USD carry. The UK-US 2Y yield spread sits at -13bp, with 5D momentum moving -30bp and 20D moving -26bp in favor of USD. CFTC data shows GBP Leveraged Funds net long at +18,698 (pctl 60), down -21,663 contracts WoW as institutional longs trim exposure following the BoE hold. Options exhibit a mild put skew with 25d Risk Reversals at -0.42 and IV at 4.8% vs HV30 at 4.0% (+0.8% VRP). Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD, technical resistance and negative 2Y yield momentum weigh on price. Catalyst: Next BoE rate decision on 5 November. Risk: UK inflation prints trigger aggressive BoE hike repricing.
